# Hinoki game fixes
#
# Recommended settings per game. The app downloads this file when the library opens and applies a
# game's line when it starts, unless the player has given that game settings of their own.
# Edit it on GitHub: everyone gets the change the next time they open the app, no new build needed.
#
# One line per game:   TITLE_ID  setting=value  setting=value  | note shown in the game's settings
#
# Settings: memory-mapping, native-buffer, surface-sync, high-accuracy, async-shaders, texture-cache,
#           shader-cache, fps-hack, cpu-opt, stretch, fast-cpu, accurate-cpu, precise-math,
#           vertex-realign, v-sync (on/off), resolution (0.5 to 4), screen-filter (Nearest, Bilinear, Bicubic, FXAA)
#           precise-math=on: no Metal fast math at all (lighting that is too bright or flickers)
#           vertex-realign=off: only if a game's models break since vertex realignment (v1.2.0)
# Lines starting with # are ignored.

# Gravity Rush (US, EU): without surface sync the bloom builds up and scenes are far too bright
PCSA00011 surface-sync=on | Surface sync on: fixes the over-bright bloom (Vita3K/compatibility#177)
PCSF00024 surface-sync=on | Surface sync on: fixes the over-bright bloom (Vita3K/compatibility#177)

# Persona 4 Golden (US, EU): vertex spikes in 3D scenes with GPU memory mapping
PCSE00120 memory-mapping=off precise-math=on | GPU memory mapping off: removes the spikes in 3D scenes. Precise shader math: for the white ground in the rainy morning scene (fast maths can turn lighting into NaN, drawn white)
PCSB00245 memory-mapping=off precise-math=on | GPU memory mapping off: removes the spikes in 3D scenes. Precise shader math: for the white ground in the rainy morning scene (fast maths can turn lighting into NaN, drawn white)

# Madden NFL 13: players are skinned on the GPU (needs memory mapping). Surface sync on: what the GPU draws
# into textures (sky, crowd, sideline lighting, stadium screens) only reaches the game with it; without it some
# stadiums show a plain blue sky, empty stands and black sideline players. It used to write a 16-bit surface
# kept as RGBA8 at twice its size over game data (0xFF000A0C pointers, a freeze loading into a game); such
# surfaces are no longer synced. surface-sync-safe: builds without that guard ignore it and keep surface sync off
PCSE00084 memory-mapping=on native-buffer=on surface-sync=off surface-sync-safe=on high-accuracy=off async-shaders=on cpu-opt=on fast-cpu=off | Native buffer and surface sync: sky, crowd and sideline players drawn into textures show up; background shaders; high accuracy off

# LittleBigPlanet: device lost at boot with memory mapping + double buffer; Sackboy invisible with mapping off.
# Same recipe as Madden (GPU-skinned characters): mapping with native buffer and surface sync
PCSA00017 memory-mapping=on native-buffer=on surface-sync=on async-shaders=on | Memory mapping with Native buffer: Sackboy is drawn by the GPU from mapped memory (invisible with mapping off), and mapping failed at boot only with Double buffer. Surface sync on: grey/white screen without it (Vita3K/compatibility#188). Background shaders for fewer hitches
PCSF00021 memory-mapping=on native-buffer=on surface-sync=on async-shaders=on | Memory mapping with Native buffer: Sackboy is drawn by the GPU from mapped memory (invisible with mapping off), and mapping failed at boot only with Double buffer. Surface sync on: grey/white screen without it (Vita3K/compatibility#188). Background shaders for fewer hitches

# Killzone Mercenary: same game ran at ~40 FPS with these settings and ~19 FPS with page-table mapping,
# high accuracy and surface sync on (owner's logs)
PCSA00107 memory-mapping=on native-buffer=off surface-sync=off high-accuracy=off fps-hack=on cpu-opt=on | Double-buffer memory mapping with surface sync and high accuracy off: about twice the frame rate in testing


# Mobile Suit Gundam: Extreme VS-Force (US, EU, Asia, JP): names, menus and the battle-start banner leave
# trails that never fade (pause screen, lock-on names). Started with v1.4.0, which turned Fast CPU on by
# default: the game's fades are float maths that the shortcuts break. Exact floating point for this game
PCSE00915 fast-cpu=off surface-sync=off high-accuracy=off fps-hack=off | Exact floating point: fixes names and menus leaving trails (broke with Fast CPU on by default in v1.4.0)
PCSB00983 fast-cpu=off surface-sync=off high-accuracy=off fps-hack=off | Exact floating point: fixes names and menus leaving trails (broke with Fast CPU on by default in v1.4.0)
PCSH00196 fast-cpu=off surface-sync=off high-accuracy=off fps-hack=off | Exact floating point: fixes names and menus leaving trails (broke with Fast CPU on by default in v1.4.0)
PCSG00738 fast-cpu=off surface-sync=off high-accuracy=off fps-hack=off | Exact floating point: fixes names and menus leaving trails (broke with Fast CPU on by default in v1.4.0)

# Dragon Ball Z: Battle of Z: voices are CRI audio decoded in software with floating point. Fast CPU
# (floating-point shortcuts, on by default in v1.4.0) garbles them; forced off even with the player's settings
PCSE00305 fast-cpu=off high-accuracy=off | Exact floating point: clean voice lines (the voice decoder is floating point); high accuracy off for speed

# Borderlands 2: high accuracy only slows it down
PCSE00383 high-accuracy=off | High accuracy off: faster, nothing it draws needs it
